subject.title: fix(vydra): stop hanging when generated asset downloads drip forever

question: Should response-body limit readers become a documented Plugin SDK runtime surface for bundled plugins such as Vydra, and if so through which public barrel or injected helper?
rationale: The timeout logic is mechanically sound, but choosing a durable SDK exposure point changes the supported plugin contract and should not be inferred from an internal-looking subpath.

options.title: Publish a narrow runtime reader surface
options.body: Expose the existing response readers through the documented Plugin SDK runtime boundary, then update Vydra to consume that public contract.

options.title: Inject a generic helper instead
options.body: Keep the readers internal and provide the capability through Vydra's runtime dependencies if that is the preferred plugin architecture.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Defer the Vydra fix until the Plugin SDK owner chooses whether this capability should be supported externally.

recommendation.title: Publish a narrow runtime reader surface
recommendation.body: Expose the existing response readers through the documented Plugin SDK runtime boundary, then update Vydra to consume that public contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the most concrete recent context on the hang-timeout implementation, although Plugin SDK ownership still needs confirmation from repository history.
